How long does the Via del Cifalco take?

The Antica Via del Cifalco can be conceived as a made-to-measure journey. Bearing in mind that it covers about 75 kilometres and 2,800 metres of ascent, nobody is advised to set out intending to complete the whole walk in fewer than three nights.

The most experienced walkers can indeed cover it in three nights, although in that case it will be hard to plan any detours. Should this be your choice, it becomes practically unavoidable to walk in one go from Ponte Organasco or Cerignale all the way to the Valico di Fregarolo, since (equipped) intermediate stopping points are hard to come by.

A far more reasonable measure for enjoying the route is four nights. This also allows you to linger along a few detours, in particular those needed to reach overnight accommodation, which may require significant departures from the route during the first part of the walk (Casanova and Ottone).

Five nights is an ideal length: if you are a good walker, it may be enough to enjoy all, or almost all, of the detours; if you are less experienced, it still lets you take everything more calmly and immerse yourself in the silence of the Via; or, why not, take a day of complete rest and contemplation in the middle of the walk.

Use the “walking tracker” below to tailor the itinerary that suits you!

Detailed description of the itinerary

Below is the detailed description of the route for hiking purposes. The sections of the main trail are grouped here purely as a guide, since each belongs to the same waymark: they can be combined and split up differently.

For each section, the corresponding detours are suggested. Where not already indicated by signs of another kind, the detours are marked by wooden signs painted in white, introducing each detour with the words “Uscita AVC:” (AVC exit).

The times given are meant for “average” hikers, albeit experienced ones.

Key: Main route Detour Variant

Ponte Organasco (457 m a.s.l.) – Cerignale (725 m a.s.l.) – Oneto (811 m a.s.l.)

From the Locanda Rosa in Ponte Organasco, walk a few metres along the paved road towards Genoa. On the left begins a wide cart track, the start of our walk.

After a few metres you reach a fountain where three ways part. Take the leftmost one, which climbs first to Carisasca and then to Castello. At Cerignale, take the trail on the right, just before reaching the Albergo del Pino. 1h of climbing to Cerignale plus 40 minutes to Oneto (20 of them on paved road):

(Alternatively, if you want to skip Cerignale and save time: the trail with the waymark that climbs - coming from Piacenza, just after the inn on the left - reaching Abrà - La Serra - Oneto. It crosses the paved road twice, arriving at Oneto in about 45 minutes from Ponte Organasco, without passing through Cerignale.)

Time: 1.40h

Waymarks: [“Anello dei Borghi”, soon to be created, as far as Cerignale and then] trail from Cerignale to Oneto.

Variant: for those who wish to reach Oneto more quickly without passing through Cerignale (thereby losing its facilities, however), from Ponte Organasco (again after the Locanda Rosa, on the left coming from Piacenza) you can follow the waymark straight away, reaching first Abrà, then La Serra, crossing the paved road twice, and finally Oneto. Time: 45 minutes.

Oneto – Slopes of Monte delle Tane

After 50 minutes you reach the junction with the trail. Before this junction, having passed two birdwatching posts (both on the left), ignore a crossroads where a trail is marked on the right with a non-CAI waymark, a white rectangle with a red central band. Carry straight on instead. Just below the junction, taking the trail on the left for a few hundred metres, is the Rifugio Casermetta, unequipped but with a spring. From the junction, our route instead carries straight on towards M. delle Tane: there, the trail “dissolves” into the trail. In 5 minutes from the junction you reach the slopes of Monte delle Tane.

Time: 55 minutes

Waymarks: and

Detour – from the slopes of M. delle Tane to the summit: A fine grassy summit with views over the whole Cifalco! The path to the top is conspicuous, about 5 minutes after the junction with the trail, on the left. Time: 10 minutes up and down

From the slopes of M. delle Tane to the slopes of M. Dego

From the slopes of M. delle Tane, the trail continues as far as the Bivio Veri (1080 m a.s.l., 1.15h from the slopes of M. delle Tane). The continuation of the trail is clearly visible if you take the paved road on the right for a few metres, towards Ottone, and then find it again immediately on the left.

You reach the summit of M. Veri (1223 m a.s.l., neither marked nor visible), and shortly afterwards meet the junction with the trail (35 minutes from the Bivio Veri). At this fork, turn left.

From here, in 20 minutes you reach the junction with the vehicle track to M. Dego. Here too, keep left.

After another 20 minutes, the vehicle track forks conspicuously: neither of the two ways is the right one! Instead, a few metres before this fork, follow the CAI waymarks that clamber up on the right (with a barely visible sign for M. Dego). In any case, even taking the right-hand vehicle track you will reach your destination, simply adding about 10 minutes.

Once you have clambered up on the right, keep right again; in particular, after 5 minutes of climbing from the junction there is another one, barely visible but marked. After a few hundred metres, the trail returns to the vehicle track left earlier. Avoid the road that descends into the woods on the right: look instead at the vehicle track on the left and take it to the right.

From the junction for Toveraia/Ottone, in 10 minutes you reach the slopes of M. Dego.

Time: 3h

Waymarks: , ,

Detours – Ottone Soprano, Ottone and Cariseto: after about 25 minutes’ walk from the slopes of M. delle Tane, you cross the trail, which leads to Ottone Soprano (1h) and Ottone (1.30h) on the right, and to Cariseto (30 minutes) on the left.

Detours – Toveraia and Ottone: about 40 minutes after the first junction with the vehicle track to M. Dego, you can see – beyond a pasture gate – the trail descending to Toveraia in 1.30h and to Ottone in 2h. From the same spot, on the opposite side of the road, an unmarked and very rough path leads to the summit of M. Dego in a few minutes, but we recommend carrying straight on and reaching the summit by the normal route.

Detour – Summit of M. Dego (1427 m a.s.l.), on the left by the mountain hut of the same name (10 minutes up and down).

From the slopes of M. Dego to the Passo di Vallersone

From the slopes of M. Dego, in 1h you reach the Rifugio Prati di Foppiano (no beds, only the possibility of cooking on site and taking shelter inside).

Once you meet the waymark, you do not leave it again: 5 minutes after the Rifugio Prati di Foppiano you come to a junction, where you go left. In 30 minutes from the hut you reach the Passo Vallersone (wrongly referred to as the “Passo Montarlone” on a plaque on the right, in yellow paint).

Time: 1.30h

Waymarks: and

Detour – Summit of M. Oramara: From the Rifugio del M. Dego, follow the waymark. Branching off it on the left (not very obvious) is the trail, which climbs through the beech wood to take us in 15 minutes to the summit of M. Oramara (1522 m a.s.l., the highest summit on the whole route).

Detour – Fontana del Figliolo: turning right at the first junction after the Rifugio Prati di Foppiano, you reach the Fontana del Figliolo in 20 minutes along an unmarked path.

Detour – Summit of Montarlone (1501 m a.s.l.). From the same junction, it is best to go left if you want to tackle the summit of Montarlone: if you go right (and then immediately left) you can reach the summit more quickly, but the path is neither marked nor visible. It is therefore not a recommended option, unless you have GPS and/or already know the route. To tackle the summit of Montarlone, follow instead the way to the Passo Vallersone; a few minutes before the pass, a trail marked climbs and in about an hour comfortably takes you to the summit, with its iconic cross and a marvellous view over Val Trebbia and Val d’Aveto.

Detour – Casanova di Rovegno. From the Passo Vallersone (where a plaque wrongly calls it “Passo Montarlone”), a spectacular trail, passing a swarm of springs and the Fontana del Vino, reaches Casanova in 1.30h. Waymarks: . Allow 2h for the climb back. NB: on the way back up, the waymark is less visible than on the way down. In particular, just after passing the first pasture gate, keep right on the nearly level road and not left towards the road that climbs.

Detour – Fontanigorda (from Casanova). From the church of Casanova, facing the façade, a descent starts on the left, marked with a red and white rectangular waymark (with a diagonal line through it), and further on also marked as a yellow cross (a “+” sign). On reaching the Pescia stream, turn right, cross the bridge and continue a few hundred metres on the tarmac. You soon cross the “Strada di Chiavari”: if you take it to the right, in a few minutes you reach a fine mill, opposite the spectacular Ponte di Canfernasca, a jewel of Roman architecture and the symbol of the Comune of Rovegno; taking it to the left instead, in about 15 minutes you reach the Bosco delle Fate and, in another 5 following the paved road, Fontanigorda. Total from Casanova: 25 minutes down, 30 up.

From the Passo di Vallersone to Barbagelata

Back on the ridge, and turning right on reaching the Passo Vallersone, the waymark leads in succession to the Passo Ertola (1287 m a.s.l., 15 minutes), the Passo Esola (1307 m a.s.l., another 15 minutes), up to the junction for the summit of M. Roccabruna (1330 m a.s.l., 30 minutes from the Passo Esola) and the one for M. Gifarco (5 minutes after the junction for the summit of M. Roccabruna). NB: the start of the path to the summit of M. Gifarco, which does not coincide with the Passo Gifarco reached a few minutes later, is really hard to see if you come from the Passo Esola – there is only a sign placed for those coming from the Passo Gifarco. The trail continues to the Passo Gifarco and the Passo del Fante (10 minutes from the slopes of M. Gifarco) and then to the Valico del Fregarolo (50 minutes from the Passo del Fante).

From the Valico del Fregarolo, the trail reaches the Passo della Rocca (1250 m a.s.l.) in 1.10h, passing the Lago della Nave. From the Passo della Rocca, the waymark continues right towards Aia di Gallo, Canale and Due Ponti, all destinations that it abandons 5 minutes later to continue on the left.

From the Passo della Rocca, the trail reaches Barbagelata passing the little chapel of Cardenosa (in good condition, 30 minutes from the Passo della Rocca) and that of Costa Finale (in complete ruin, 50 minutes from the Cappelletta di Cardenosa). Between the two chapels, near Monte Pietrabianca, the sea comes into view on the left for the first time. From the Cappelletta di Costa Finale, you reach Barbagelata (1115 m a.s.l.) in 30 minutes. NB: about 5 minutes after the ruins of the Cappelletta di Costa Finale, pay the utmost attention because the waymark continues on the right along a narrower path than the main one.

Time: 4.05h

Waymarks:

Detour – Rezzoaglio: from the Passo Ertola, descending to the left, you come first to Ertola and then to Rezzoaglio (waymark , 50 minutes down, 1.10h up).

Detour – Summit of M. Roccabruna (1415 m a.s.l.): from the junction for the summit, 15 minutes up, 10 down, waymark faded in places, but visible; in theory, at a certain point you could cut across to the summit of M. Gifarco without returning to the junction, but the starting point is unclear and the time saved is minimal.

Detour – Summit of M. Gifarco (1380 m a.s.l.): from the slopes of M. Gifarco, an extremely steep ascent (and descent!), often slippery, even on fine days. Although it is not equipped with chains, the last stretch of path, inside a rocky gully, may require the use of your hands. Allow 10 minutes to climb and another 10 to descend back to the junction. Waymark .

Detour – Trattoria Al Valico near the Passo del Fregarolo: five minutes from the Passo del Fregarolo, on the right, you come across the trattoria.

From Barbagelata (1150 m a.s.l.) to Neirone (342 m a.s.l.)

From Barbagelata, continue along the paved road to the edge of the village. An obvious junction marks the crossing with the Alta Via dei Monti Liguri, which you can take either to the right or to the left. We suggest taking it to the left (that is, eastwards), gently downhill towards the Passo della Scoglina (920 m a.s.l.), which you reach in 15 minutes (waymark , but also “A13” and “AV”). From the pass, recognisable by the meeting of three paved roads that intersect there, take the uphill trail that climbs at one o’clock (waymark and “A13”) which, after several fords across the streams that form the first stretches of the Aveto, leads to the Acquapendente (1075 m a.s.l.) in 1.15h from the pass. From there begins a steep and tiring climb that in about 30 minutes leads to the summit of Monte Caucaso (1245 m a.s.l., waymark ) and its fine mountain hut/restaurant, with a 360-degree view over the whole Ligurian Apennines, the Valle Fontanabuona, the Valle del Malvaro and the whole Tigullio.

From the summit of M. Caucaso, follow the ridge westwards (the sea on our left) which, after a first downhill ramp, climbs steeply towards the “Caucasino” and descends in about 1h to the locality of Faggio Rotondo (waymark ). NB: after leaving the Passo di Pietra Cavallina, descending to the left with a sharp hairpin bend, within a few minutes the trail begins to be flanked by dry-stone walls on both sides. From there, you need to keep your eyes open because – about 40 minutes in all from the start of the descent from the summit of M. Caucaso – the waymark suddenly veers right, towards an abandoned house that you must walk round clockwise to pick up the trail again towards Faggio Rotondo, which you reach through chestnut woods and expanses of ferns.

From Faggio Rotondo, the waymark continues via Pian del Pero (30 minutes from Faggio Rotondo). NB: this is the part of the whole route where the waymark is least visible, since it is structurally subject to “invasions” by vegetation in spring. At Pian del Pero, the meets the paved road again and follows it – with “shortcuts” across the bends – as far as the Cascina Arsena (not signposted, but clearly recognisable since it is the only one on the route, just below the road). From there, the trail leaves the paved road and descends straight to the centre of the village of Neirone (30 minutes from Pian del Pero).

NB: from Barbagelata, taking the Alta Via to the right instead of the left (that is, westwards instead of eastwards) saves some ascent and also – considerably – some time, as it cuts directly to the summit of M. Caucaso with about 45 minutes less. If you consider the direct descent to Neirone without passing over the summit of M. Caucaso, the saving is as much as 1h compared with the recommended itinerary; however, you thereby lose the spectacular climb to the Caucaso along the ridge between Aveto and Malvaro, as well as the Acquapendente. This is a shortcut recommended only for those who need to make do with shorter walking times, or for those who must make up time lost during earlier stages of the crossing.

Time: 4h

Waymarks: , “A13” as far as the Acquapendente; as far as the summit of the Caucaso; as far as Neirone

Detour – from Cascina Arsena to B&B Ca’ da Nonna (the only place for refreshment and overnight accommodation in Neirone, apart from Faggio Rotondo): follow the paved road instead of the trail for about 15 minutes (about 30 from Pian del Pero). From there, right in front of the B&B, an unmarked road passes two gates (to be opened and closed again) and, through scrub running along a boundary, you rejoin the paved road, to be taken to the left downhill. With more or less obvious shortcuts, this leads to Neirone village in 25 minutes from the B&B.

Detour – Roccatagliata: about 1h’s walk following the provincial road uphill or the Itinerario dei Feudi Fliscani (IFF) to the right. In the latter case, check that it is passable.

From Neirone to the Passo dei Casetti (549 m a.s.l.)

From Neirone, at the main junction of the village, you descend to Gattorna in about 50 minutes. From the car park beside the Church of Neirone, at the foot of the flight of steps leading to the town hall, itself the starting point of many hiking itineraries, you can join the “Itinerario dei Feudi Fliscani” (waymark “IFF” on a blue and yellow rectangle), taking it to the left (climbing to the right, it would instead lead to M. Lavagnola). Although it is the subject of restoration works currently under way and structurally in need of constant maintenance, the IFF has recently been made passable as part of the Antica Via del Cifalco project. It nevertheless remains possible to follow, as an alternative, the paved road from Neirone to Gattorna should the condition of the trail suddenly worsen.

You pass the Sanctuary of Nostra Signora della Guardia di Gattorna, which overlooks the village, and descend – by one of the many lanes or flights of steps – to the main street crossed by the state road (SS 225), which runs parallel to the Lavagna stream. Walk up this main street for a few hundred metres, until you spot the small lane on the left, also paved, which, between the Pasticceria Torre and the bar La Ciuccheria, descends to the little wooden bridge over the Lavagna stream. Here the waymark begins.

After the bridge, keep left, avoiding the road that climbs straight away towards Pian dei Preti; then cross the old little stone bridge over the Rio Rosso. The trail, cutting across the tarmac several times, passes through Cassanesi and leads to the Passo dei Casetti (550 m a.s.l., 1.40h from Gattorna), recognisable by the characteristic bridge above the trail. The waymark stops when it meets the Itinerario Storico Colombiano (ISC, with a white and red waymark), coming from Garbarini and Terrarossa Colombo. Take the ISC to the right, walking the last 10 minutes before the Passo dei Casetti under the aegis of the ISC waymark.

NB: although passable at the time this itinerary was written, the little wooden bridge at Gattorna is not perfectly maintained: check that there are no closure orders and, if there are, go round by the paved bridge that descends to the stream from the Bar Beneitin; once over the bridge, turn right and, after a few hundred metres, pick up again the waymark that climbs on the left.

NB: near Cassanesi, you will notice on the right a fine house in a state of ruin, a few dozen metres from the trail. Although the stretch is perfectly passable, the Comune of Tribogna has issued order no. 19 of 16 December 2025 prohibiting passage along the trail on that stretch; should this order still be in force at the time of your hike, complying with it would mean going back down a few hundred metres to the last crossing with the paved road (to be taken to the right for those turning back, to the left for those climbing) and then picking up the waymark again after the trattoria Madia, on the right.

Time: 2.30h

Waymarks: paved road from Neirone to Gattorna (no waymark); as far as the junction with the ISC; white and red ISC waymark as far as the Passo dei Casetti

Detour – Colle Caprile: from the Passo dei Casetti, the waymark of the Via del Sale/Via del Mare (followed in reverse) lets you go to Colle Caprile in 40 minutes, where there is food and accommodation (“Albergo Caprile”).

Detour – Uscio: from the Passo dei Casetti, passing under the little bridge and keeping right, you reach Uscio in about 30 minutes (waymark ). In Uscio, a characteristic little village of the Ligurian hinterland, there are plenty of options for accommodation and food.

Variant: from Neirone, you can descend to Gattorna on the paved road, in about 50 minutes. This is the recommended option should landslides, collapses or other events occur on the IFF that limit its passability. In any case, the IFF, descending towards Gattorna, crosses the vehicle road shortly before the power station, so you can also opt for the paved road as an escape route.

From the Passo dei Casetti to Portofino Mare

From the pass, our trail follows in its entirety the last stretch of the Via del Sale/Via del Mare, with the characteristic white and red “VM” signs, which can therefore be used as a reference in addition to the ordinary FIE waymarks. The waymark reaches the Passo Spinarola in 40 minutes. It is hard to understand why the waymark first descends towards Uscio, forcing you first into a not very obvious turn to the left 5 minutes after the Passo dei Casetti and, a little further on, into 20 minutes of paved road as far as the Colonia Arnaldi; all this could have been avoided by easily routing the waymark towards the far more panoramic M. Tugio, taking the trail that climbs immediately on the left from the Passo dei Casetti, before passing under the bridge, and then descending to the Passo della Spinarola. In any case, the Via del Sale/Via del Mare – wisely, all the same – follows in the footsteps of the FIE waymark and so will our itinerary. The more adventurous may still try the path that goes over M. Tugio, but only if they have GPS or know the area thoroughly, since the track is not marked. NB: for those determined to spare themselves the dismal visit to the Colonia Arnaldi without venturing onto M. Tugio, there is a shortcut – also unmarked – which, right by the “Benvenuti” (Welcome) sign at the entrance to the Colonia, climbs on the left with a signpost for the Passo Spinarola. A few metres before this pass, it rejoins the waymark.

The way continues to the Passo del Gallo (55 minutes from the Passo Spinarola), the Piane di Caravaggio (30 minutes from the Passo del Gallo), up to the “Millenaria” (thousand-year-old) Church of Ruta (55 minutes from the Piane di Caravaggio).

From the “Millenaria”, take the paved road on the right for about 10 minutes, until you arrive in the centre of Ruta, at the point where it crosses the busy Via Aurelia. Here the trail ends. Once in front of the benches with a view of the sea, turn left; just past the bar Egidio, again on the left – just before the tunnel – appears the sign with the waymark at the beginning of a flight of steps climbing towards the Church of San Michele.

Leaving this on your left, you see, on the right, the turning for the trail to Portofino Mare (5 minutes from the crossing with the Aurelia, waymark ). At that point, you enter the Parco del M. di Portofino. In 2.15h from the last sign in Ruta, you reach Portofino Mare via the Sella della Gaixella, Pietre Strette and San Sebastiano. NB: Santa Margherita Ligure station can be reached from here by a lovely trail ( as far as Paraggi, then along the seafront) in about 1.15h from Portofino Mare.

Time: 5.15h

Waymarks: as far as Ruta; as far as Portofino Mare

Detour – Passo della Serra and Manico del Lume: from the slopes of M. Bello, the FIE waymark leads in 1h to the Passo della Serra and in 1.30h to the Manico del Lume. NB: for the ascent to the summit section of the Manico del Lume there are chains, so the trail is graded for experienced and equipped hikers (EEA). If you wish, the same trail also leads to the Sanctuary of Montallegro in 3.30h, but this, rather than a detour, should be considered an outing in its own right.

Detour – Sanctuary of Caravaggio: from the Piane di Caravaggio, the waymark, on the left, leads to the Sanctuary of Caravaggio in about 20 minutes.

Detour – Recco: after about 45 minutes’ walk from the Piane di Caravaggio, a trail sets off on the right and descends to Recco in 1h (waymark ).

Detour – San Rocco – Camogli – Punta Chiappa: on the way between Ruta and Portofino, past Portofino Vetta, the waymark branches off on the right and descends to San Rocco in about 45 minutes. From there, you can descend to Punta Chiappa for a memorable swim (in about 40 minutes, waymark ) or to Camogli (in about 25 minutes, via the waymark), where there is a railway station.

Detour – San Fruttuoso: from the crossroads of Pietre Strette, take on the right the old mule track to San Fruttuoso, marked by the waymark. You reach your destination in about 1h, passing, among other things, the Agririfugio Molini.

Detour – Santa Margherita Ligure: shortly after Pietre Strette, on the left, the waymark sets off and, in about 50 minutes, leads to Santa Margherita Ligure.

Detour – Nozarego: after 1.30h’s walk from Ruta on the way to Portofino, at the locality of Crocetta a trail branches off on the left that leads to Nozarego in 45 minutes, waymark . NB: from Nozarego there are various ways down to Santa Margherita, including a paved road.

Map and GPX track

Below is the interactive map of the Antica Via del Cifalco, available in GPX format. It can also be downloaded from the main hiking apps around (those that use the “OpenStreetMap” interface).

To stay on the right path, always and only refer to the CAI waymarks (white and red marks) and the FIE waymarks (geometric shapes – yellow on the “continental” stretch and red on the “maritime” one).

Our logo appears only occasionally along the route and is not meant to replace the official waymarking. Moreover, it is posted only on the main trail: do not look for it if you are on a detour or a variant.
